measurement_scope: isolated component fixture, two normal convene/two-round/close paths with scripted Research HTTP boundary; not hosted measurements

hosted_scale_basis.human_convened: H additional meetings/day, counted separately; existing caller/operator budget overrides are not assumed zero

measured.source: measurements.txt; sizes use JSON default ASCII encoding, ledger includes formatting

lanes: accepted updated since last fully read same-series review
read_bounds.capability_reads_per_execution_attempt: one per participant before rounds (at most 5), plus one per explicitly adopted Persona action (at most 8), with that action's own required_data, not a union per participant; frozen-close retries do not re-query
read_bounds.case_file_items: existing four groups at 8 each plus at most 24 action citation items; original excerpt/subject-field total 12000 characters plus at most 9600 action excerpt characters
read_bounds.provider_calls: existing at most 16 per meeting; two rounds normally, third only with chair evidence
read_bounds.pagination: One whole ticket per lane, at most eight refs each (24 reads total), no partial evidence cache. Successful ticket pages advance independently even when evidence is unavailable; failed ticket pages retain their own cursor. At most three completed-lane names and one sticky evidence-failure flag persist alongside three 128-character cursors and the original scan start. Completed lanes wait for traversal completion. On any evidence failure the completed traversal clears cursors but retains the old watermark for a fair retry; otherwise the inclusive watermark advances only to the first page start. Concurrent earlier-key changes are revisited next scan; bare legacy cursors restart safely.
read_bounds.live_action_detail_reads: at most 8 current plus 3 prior direct owner reads per detail request; legacy proposal status reads remain a separate existing cost
read_bounds.throughput: At most one ticket per lane per same-series meeting; N stable tickets in a lane require N meetings per traversal. At nine scheduled meetings/week across three personas this is at most 27 prior-ticket slots/week (nine per lane), plus up to 3*H/day from human meetings. No latency or hosted throughput acceptance is claimed. The smaller ticket page ensures every selected ticket can receive all eight evidence reads in one meeting.
read_bounds.schedule_reads: One exact tenant/chair/meeting-type/stable-series projection lookup, restored by existing active detail for HTTP execution. Independent projection is derived from existing schedule lifecycle events on normal append/replay, including prior events overwritten in the cadence slot. No read-time archive scan, extra endpoint or owner call; frozen/closed meetings retain recorded state.

existing_writers.name: consultation meeting lifecycle records
existing_writers.cadence: existing convene, pre-read, round, synthesis, close and explicit workflow retries; no new timer
existing_writers.counts: at most 8 adopted actions and 8 reviews per meeting; at most 3 prior snapshots and 24 resolved evidence contents; bounded references only, mutable progress remains at Research
existing_writers.growth_per_day_measured_model: logical latest records about 16677 + 12971*H bytes/day; lifecycle append bytes about 134070 + 104276*H/day and 25.1 + 19.5*H events/day for this measured two-participant workload (rounded up)
existing_writers.maximum_scale: new actions at most 72/week plus 8*H/day; request/case/section caps above apply also to separately counted human work; physical growth depends on actual participants, rounds, evidence, retries and pre-existing content, so the measured model is not a maximum
existing_writers.cap_and_cleanup: existing four-group case budget plus 256 KiB encoded case and 2 MiB encoded provider request enforced; reference caps enforced before persistence/dispatch. No whole-history retention or cleanup verified; inherited RC3 WP3.1/3.3 debt, no deletion/backfill of open or historical obligations

existing_writers.name: meeting_output_dispatches.json
existing_writers.cadence: two upserts per attempted new action/review (frozen request then genuine receipt), at most 32 upserts per meeting with 8 creations and 8 reviews; successful replay is read-only
existing_writers.counts: one existing-ledger row per tenant/meeting/source action or tenant/reviewing meeting/ticket; POST omits ticket_id; no second ID hash
existing_writers.growth_per_day_measured_model: about 3220 + 2505*H bytes/day for this measured two-action/one-review workload; failed retries replace their existing row
existing_writers.cap_and_cleanup: bounded request/reference/receipt envelopes; owner enforces 8 assignments/origin and 16 KiB command/assignment. Existing ledger has no whole-file cap or retention and rewrites the archive atomically; RC3 owner retains that debt

existing_writers.name: existing meeting_schedule
existing_writers.cadence: existing successful meeting close, at most 5 participant updates/meeting
existing_writers.counts: Existing tenant/persona/meeting_type cadence key and event payload unchanged. Derived in-memory review index has S entries for distinct (tenant, chair, meeting_type, stable series), with only series, watermark, three bounded cursors/completed lanes, scan-start and failure flag per value. Only chair writes carry review progress; peer cadence merges preserve it. Latest cadence projection still has one entry per original key.
existing_writers.growth_per_day: No extra persistent row/event/byte per close: existing at most 45 schedule lifecycle updates/week (6.43/day) plus 5*H/day. Derived index adds at most one entry per newly chaired stable series (at most 9/week or 1.29/day plus H/day at the hosted meeting budget, repeated series add zero). S entries survive replay; no unfinished entry evicted. Python heap size is unmeasured; JSON generated review value is at most 8011 bytes for the measured maximal astral-subject/cursor fixture, 971 with ASCII equivalents; tuple keys and Python overhead are additional.
existing_writers.cap_and_cleanup: Per-value bounds: stable subject <=256 characters, at most three <=128-character owner cursors, three fixed completed-lane labels, UTC timestamps and one boolean. Original meeting/provider caps unchanged. Continuation clears per series only after traversal; watermark advances only to original scan-start on complete source/evidence reads. No global S cap/cleanup verified: derived index grows with supported stable subjects and inherits RC3 lifecycle retention debt. It cannot discard unfinished series. Future lifecycle compaction must retain each series checkpoint, not just the latest cadence slot. No new timer, file, table or migration; JSONL/PostgreSQL normal replay restores the index without writes.
